problem: The clause "left in place it steals area from one side and adds it to the other" describes a transfer of area between the two neighbours. A sliver is a separate thin polygon sitting between two boundaries that should coincide; it holds a strip that belongs to neither neighbour, so both neighbours lose area to it and the layer's total area is inflated. The quiz answer repeats the same wrong transfer picture, which a student could carry into an overlay exercise.
fix: Write: "A sliver has no real owner; left in place it takes a strip of area from the polygons on both sides and adds a false polygon to the layer, so every area total and every overlay is wrong." In the Q2 answer use the same wording.

problem: "Four points allow an affine fit" is misleading about the minimum: an affine transformation has six unknowns (two shifts, two scales, two rotations/shears), so three control points already give a unique exact fit. Four points give a redundant least-squares affine fit.
fix: "Three control points give the minimum exact affine fit; four or more give a redundant affine fit whose residuals can be checked. Six or more allow a second-order polynomial fit that absorbs scanner distortion."

problem: The answer presents dangle and undershoot as if they were separate kinds of error. The free endpoint left by an undershoot is itself a dangling node in the topology, so a student may think an undershoot does not show up as a dangle.
fix: Add one sentence: "In the built topology the free endpoint of an undershoot is recorded as a dangling node, so dangles are the symptom and overshoot/undershoot the cause."
